newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss eye Euro-denominated stock segment - CS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss eye Euro-denominated stock segment - CS.

text.p: The Swiss Exchange is drawing up plans to introduce a special segment in which Swiss companies can have their shares traded in euros as well as in Swiss francs, bankers from Credit Suisse said on Tuesday.
The Swiss Interbank Clearing system is also eyeing the possibility of clearing euro payments as well as Swiss francs if the single European currency proves to be a success, they said.
"We may well have to live for a longer period with two parallel currencies," Credit Suisse analyst Fritz Stahel told an Institute for International Research seminar on the euro.

If the euro was stable and won international stature, Swiss firms would have to issue invoices and keep accounts in euros even though Switzerland did not take part, he said. It would also be used in retail trade near borders and in tourist areas.
"We assume as a bank that large companies will quickly start thinking in euros," he said.

"There are already concrete plans that the Swiss Interbank Clearing...will -- in addition to the Swiss franc as basis currency -- develop a special pipeline that allows euro payments so that we are competitive," he explained.
It remained an open question whether Swiss banks would have access to the EU's TARGET clearing system, he said.
Large companies would also be interested in having their shares quoted in euros, Stahel said, noting some might be tempted to do this in Frankfurt or other EU financial centres.

"But we want to keep this business in Switzerland and here as well the exchange has concrete plans to create a euro segment on the Swiss Exchange where companies have the possibility of having their shares listed in euros," he said.
